html:
Unreal / Blender handoff

This implements the first manual round-trip stage of the original roadmap. It is not real-time synchronization and does not replace existing assets.

User controls

  • Blender: Send to Unreal sends the active supported static mesh through the existing preview/apply FBX workflow. The old operator identifier is retained for compatibility, but the panel, button and confirmation use the new wording.
  • Unreal: Send to Blender uses exactly one selected Content Browser static mesh, or one selected StaticMeshActor's mesh if no mesh asset is selected. The Blender object name starts blank and keeps the source static mesh asset's name. Enter a name to override it before sending. The handoff uses the mesh asset's geometry, not the selected actor's world transform.
  • Unreal: Import from Blender pulls the named Blender source mesh, or its active object when the name is blank. Choose a new /Game/.../SM_Name asset path. An existing destination is preserved and rejected with an actionable message. This imports/saves new assets without placing an actor or saving a level.

Start both bridges first. With multiple Blender sessions, enter the intended blender-PID; otherwise a single connected session is selected. The Unreal panel passes its own project registration directory to its worker, independently of the Codex client's session-discovery configuration.

Every button prepares a preview. Review the source, destination and limitations, then confirm. Cancellation during preparation/preview applies no transfer. Keep both applications open while an apply is running. An interrupted apply is uncertain; inspect its receipt and target before trying anything again.

Current supported payload

The Unreal-to-Blender route supports binary FBX and OBJ for loaded /Game/ or /JasperPrism/ static mesh assets: one mesh, LOD0, at most 100,000 source vertices, 200,000 triangles and 32 material slots. Separate high-resolution source descriptions, skeletal meshes, animation, collisions and actor/world hierarchies are excluded. OBJ also requires render LOD0 triangles to match the source mesh description. The native UE OBJ exporter writes corner-expanded vertex records and sidecars; only the main .obj is transferred. Blender welds exactly coincident vertices while retaining per-loop UVs and face smoothing data.

Unreal material graphs are not portable Blender shaders. FBX transfers receive editable opaque constant Principled placeholders. UE's OBJ exporter includes triangulated positions and UV0 but omits normals and material data; the importer recalculates geometry normals and assigns an editable placeholder. OBJ uses UE's native X-forward/Y-up/Z-right basis and centimeter coordinates; import converts to Blender -Y-forward/Z-up and the target scene's physical unit scale. These An asymmetric disposable UE 5.6.1/Blender 5.2.2 MCP fixture verified the OBJ axis and unit conversion against the full returned vertex set, bounds and triangle count. The native importer must use a negative-X forward axis for this exporter convention; the fixture caught and fixed the initial positive-X reflection. Visual/material equivalence is not claimed. The Blender return route retains its existing opaque constant-material contract: textures, procedural graphs, modifiers, parented meshes and animation require later transfer work and are rejected explicitly.

Reviewed Blender modifier edits

blender_preview_scene now accepts a typed set_modifier_settings operation for a supported existing modifier on a local mesh in Object Mode. It validates the modifier and proposed settings, then verifies the applied values by reading them back. A multi-operation recipe captures prior values and restores them if a later operation fails. Modifier state participates in object fingerprints, so a preview expires after a competing settings edit. Native MCP acceptance covered successful read-back, injected failure with rollback, and stale-preview rejection. This edits the Blender scene only; it does not make modifiers transferable in the Blender-to-Unreal mesh payload.

Stable mesh bindings

Each reviewed Blender export receives a stable 128-bit binding ID. The add-on attaches it to the source object only after the confirmed export succeeds; the .blend remains unsaved until the user saves it. Unreal imports retain that ID and the Blender source snapshot SHA-256 in package metadata. Unreal sends reuse a stored binding, or derive a stable ID from the project and asset path for an unbound source. Blender stores the ID on the received object. A disposable native MCP round trip verified the same binding through Blender → Unreal → Blender → Unreal, then restarted the Editor and verified the ID after package reload.

The source snapshot SHA-256 fingerprints the transferable content (mesh topology, geometry, supported attributes/material state, object identity, units and transform) without process-local object addresses, so it remains comparable after reopening an application. It records the Blender revision imported into that Unreal asset.

forge_compare_mesh_binding and the app-specific blender_inspect_mesh_binding and unreal_inspect_mesh_binding tools compare the current revisions with the recorded Blender and Unreal baselines. They report synchronized, blender_changed, unreal_changed, both_changed_conflict, binding_mismatch, unbound, or baseline_unavailable. These tools only inspect loaded application data and never create an apply preview, edit, or save an asset. Unreal mesh/material-slot state is fingerprinted; edits inside a referenced material graph are not currently included. The MCP round-trip acceptance run observed synchronized on both an original and a returned mesh, then observed blender_changed after a reviewed Blender transform. The other report states are covered by coordinator tests; their native Editor cases remain to be verified.

Successful import makes the received Blender mesh active for editing. It does not save the .blend file. Source Unreal assets remain unchanged during the initial import. For an existing bound mesh, the optional reviewed replacement path can reimport Blender's changed static mesh into the same Unreal asset after making and verifying a package backup and retaining existing material assignments. The replacement preview becomes stale if either side changes before apply.

Implementation boundaries

forge_preview_send_to_blender and forge_apply_send_to_blender coordinate native Unreal mesh_export_preview/mesh_export_apply with Blender import_preview/import_apply. Unreal uses native UAssetExportTask and UStaticMeshExporterFBX or UStaticMeshExporterOBJ on the Editor game thread. Blender imports through its native FBX or OBJ operator on its main thread. Neither adapter accepts arbitrary code or caller-selected artifact paths.

The external panel worker uses these MCP tools for both Unreal buttons. Existing Blender-to-Unreal MCP tools remain the implementation behind both Send to Unreal and Import from Blender. Expiring previews bind source snapshots, session authentication identities and application context. Applies are single-use.

Private generated staging retains the FBX or OBJ with size/SHA-256 verification. OBJ validation rejects non-triangle faces and all MTL/sidecar directives, so the importer never follows external paths. The shared workflow journal records export, staging, import and verification. Native import failure rolls back newly created Blender datablocks; successful stages and uncertain outcomes retain receipts. Graph/asset recovery is not implied by having a receipt. The receiving object stores its originating transfer ID, and the receipt retains the source asset and destination identity.

Loading the updated development build

The validated artifacts are Artifacts/ForgeMCP-Unreal-Development-0.2.0-UE5.6.1-Win64.zip and Artifacts/ForgeMCP-Blender-Addon-0.2.28.zip. The Unreal package requires the matching Unreal 5.6.1 Win64 build; another engine build needs a rebuild.

Save your work and close JasperPrismDev before replacing its native plugin DLL. From PowerShell, install the prepared package with:

& '[local path] `
    -ProjectFile '[local path] Engine Projects\JasperPrismDev\JasperPrismDev.uproject' `
    -PackageArchive '[local path]

The installer preserves the existing plugin/project backup and refuses replacement while that project is open. Save Blender work before closing Blender, then update the add-on from the 0.2.28 ZIP through Preferences, or use the existing source installer scripts/Install-ForgeBlender.ps1 -BlenderVersion 5.2. Reopen both apps, enable ForgeMCP, start their bridges and reconnect Codex's ForgeMCP integration. Open Unreal's Window > ForgeMCP and Blender's ForgeMCP sidebar. Choose the ForgeMCP folder containing the .venv in each panel.

The packages and MCP workflow passed disposable native acceptance. They have not been hot-replaced into the user's currently running applications. Interactive panel clicks and rendered material appearance are separate acceptance checks.

Next stages toward seamless editing

Stable identity, content fingerprints, read-only revision comparison and an explicitly reviewed Blender-to-Unreal replacement path are implemented. The replacement path was exercised through actual MCP stdio against disposable UE 5.6.1 and Blender processes. It verified a .uasset backup by SHA-256, preserved the existing material assignment, compared the bindings as synchronized, and reloaded the Editor to verify saved revision metadata. The fixture did not exercise split package sidecars, forced reimport/save failures, rollback recovery, or interactive Slate clicks; those remain open validation work.

Remaining stages:

  1. Validate broader static mesh UVs, normals, material slots and non-default units.
  2. Exercise replacement rollback/recovery failures and broader package sidecar cases.
  3. Add change detection, debouncing, conflict handling, loop suppression and an explicit live-sync switch. A change originating in one application must not bounce back indefinitely or silently replace a user's concurrent edit.
  4. Extend payloads, texture transfer, skeletal meshes and animation using separate versioned contracts and native acceptance tests.

The wider roadmap's PCG, comprehensive asset management, editor diagnostics and advanced animation/retargeting work remain separate features. This handoff stage does not mark the entire Unreal/Blender roadmap complete.
